# r2p_nest
    
```{r function-r2p_nest}
#' Row to Pair Nested Transformation
#'
#' @description
#' Pivots the levels of one column (`names_from`, e.g. environment, farm or
#' test station) into separate columns for every trait in `cols`, aligning
#' records by the identifier columns `id` (e.g. the animal ID). The result is
#' nested by trait, ready for iterative analyses such as genetic correlations
#' of the same trait across environments.
#'
#' @param data Input `data.frame` or `data.table`. It is never modified.
#' @param names_from A single column name or index whose levels become columns.
#' @param cols A character vector of column names or numeric indices: the
#'   trait columns to pivot.
#' @param id Identifier column(s) used to align rows across levels of
#'   `names_from`. Default `NULL` uses all columns that are neither in `cols`
#'   nor `names_from` (a message lists them); supplying `id` explicitly is
#'   strongly recommended.
#' @param out_type Output nesting format (`"dt"` or `"df"`). Default `"dt"`.
#'
#' @details
#' The combination of `id` and `names_from` must identify every row uniquely.
#' Otherwise `dcast()` would aggregate duplicated records with `length()` and
#' silently replace trait values by counts; the function stops instead.
#'
#' Other trait columns in `cols` are never used as identifiers: their values
#' differ between environments and would prevent any pairing.
#'
#' @return A nested `data.table` with columns `name` (trait) and `data`.
#'   Each nested table holds the `id` columns plus one column per level of
#'   `names_from`.
#'
#' @import data.table
#' @importFrom stats as.formula
#' @export
r2p_nest <- function(data,
                     names_from,
                     cols,
                     out_type = "dt",
                     id       = NULL) {

  # -- 1. Validate inputs -----------------------------------------------------
  if (!is.data.frame(data))
    stop("`data` must be a data.table or data.frame.", call. = FALSE)

  # dcast() returns new objects, so the input is never modified: no copy.
  dt <- if (data.table::is.data.table(data)) data else data.table::as.data.table(data)
  nms <- names(dt)

  names_from <- .resolve_cols(names_from, nms, "names_from")
  if (length(names_from) != 1L)
    stop("`names_from` must be a single column.", call. = FALSE)
  cols <- .resolve_cols(cols, nms, "cols")
  if (names_from %chin% cols)
    stop("`names_from` must not also appear in `cols`.", call. = FALSE)
  .check_choice(out_type, c("dt", "df"), "out_type")

  # -- 2. Identifier columns ----------------------------------------------------
  # Rows are aligned across levels of `names_from` by `id`. Other trait columns
  # must never act as identifiers: they differ between environments and would
  # prevent any pairing.
  if (is.null(id)) {
    id <- setdiff(nms, c(cols, names_from))
    if (length(id) > 0L)
      message("[ r2p_nest ] `id` not supplied; using all remaining column(s) as ",
              "identifiers: ", paste(id, collapse = ", "),
              ". Supply `id` explicitly (e.g. the animal ID) for reliable pairing.")
  } else {
    id <- .resolve_cols(id, nms, "id")
    overlap <- intersect(id, c(cols, names_from))
    if (length(overlap) > 0L)
      stop("`id` must not overlap with `cols` or `names_from`: ",
           paste(overlap, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (length(id) == 0L)
    stop("No identifier column available; supply `id`.", call. = FALSE)

  # Without uniqueness dcast() would silently aggregate with length(),
  # replacing trait values by counts.
  if (anyDuplicated(dt, by = c(id, names_from)) > 0L)
    stop("The combination of `id` (", paste(id, collapse = ", "), ") and `names_from` (",
         names_from, ") does not uniquely identify rows; dcast() would aggregate ",
         "values into counts. Check for duplicated records or supply a more ",
         "specific `id`.", call. = FALSE)

  clash <- intersect(as.character(unique(dt[[names_from]])), id)
  if (length(clash) > 0L)
    stop("Value(s) of `names_from` coincide with `id` column name(s): ",
         paste(clash, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)

  form <- stats::as.formula(sprintf(
    "%s ~ %s",
    paste(sprintf("`%s`", id), collapse = " + "),
    sprintf("`%s`", names_from)
  ))

  # -- 3. Pivot each trait --------------------------------------------------------
  result_list <- lapply(cols, function(b) {
    wide <- data.table::dcast(dt, form, value.var = b)
    if (out_type == "df") data.table::setDF(wide)
    res <- data.table::data.table(name = b)
    res[, data := list(list(wide))]
    res
  })

  data.table::rbindlist(result_list)
}
```

```{r example-r2p_nest}
# Example: the same traits recorded on the same animals in two farms
set.seed(1)
growth <- data.frame(
  animal = rep(sprintf("A%02d", 1:6), each = 2),
  farm   = rep(c("farm1", "farm2"), times = 6),
  adg    = round(rnorm(12, 900, 50)),     # average daily gain
  bf     = round(rnorm(12, 11, 1.5), 1)   # backfat
)

# Example 1: column names
r2p_nest(
  growth,
  names_from = "farm",           # levels become columns: farm1, farm2
  cols      = c("adg", "bf"),    # traits to pivot
  id        = "animal"           # aligns records of the same animal
)
# Returns a nested data.table where:
# - name: trait names (adg, bf)
# - data: one row per animal with columns animal, farm1, farm2

# Example 2: numeric indices
r2p_nest(growth, names_from = 2, cols = 3:4, id = 1)
```

```{r tests-r2p_nest}
test_that("r2p_nest aligns records of the same id across levels", {
  d <- data.frame(id = c(1, 1, 2, 2), env = c("A", "B", "A", "B"),
                  t1 = 1:4, t2 = 5:8)
  res <- r2p_nest(d, names_from = "env", cols = c("t1", "t2"), id = "id")
  expect_identical(res$name, c("t1", "t2"))
  expect_identical(as.data.frame(res$data[[1]]),
                   data.frame(id = c(1, 2), A = c(1L, 3L), B = c(2L, 4L)))
  expect_s3_class(r2p_nest(d, "env", "t1", id = "id", out_type = "df")$data[[1]],
                  "data.frame", exact = TRUE)
})

test_that("r2p_nest refuses duplicated id / names_from combinations", {
  d <- data.frame(id = c(1, 1, 2), env = c("A", "A", "B"), t1 = 1:3)
  expect_error(r2p_nest(d, "env", "t1", id = "id"), "uniquely identify")
})
```

# export_nest
    
```{r function-export_nest}
#' Export Nested Data Structures with Hierarchical Directory Organization
#'
#' @description
#' Exports list-columns containing \code{data.frame} or \code{data.table} objects from a
#' \code{data.frame}/\code{data.table} to \code{txt} or \code{csv} files, automatically
#' constructing a hierarchical directory structure from non-nested columns.
#' Exportable nested columns (those holding \code{data.frame}/\code{data.table} elements)
#' are distinguished from non-exportable custom-object columns (e.g. fitted model
#' objects); only the former are written to disk by default.
#'
#' @param data        A \code{data.frame} or \code{data.table} containing at least one
#'   nested list-column. Must have one or more rows.
#' @param by          Optional character vector of column names used to build the
#'   hierarchical output directory structure. When \code{NULL} (default), all non-nested
#'   columns are used automatically.
#' @param cols        Optional character vector of nested column names to export. When
#'   \code{NULL} (default), all columns whose elements are \code{data.frame}/\code{data.table}
#'   objects are exported automatically; custom-object list-columns are reported and skipped.
#'   Specifying a non-\code{data.frame} column triggers a warning and that column is skipped.
#' @param path        Single character string specifying the root export directory.
#'   Defaults to \code{tempdir()}. Created recursively if it does not exist.
#' @param file_type   Either \code{"txt"} (tab-separated, default) or \code{"csv"}
#'   (comma-separated). Case-insensitive.
#' @param na          Single string written for missing values. Default \code{"NA"}
#'   (\code{fwrite}'s own default, an empty field, breaks whitespace-delimited
#'   readers). Use e.g. \code{"-9999"} for DMU.
#' @param quote       Passed to \code{\link[data.table]{fwrite}}. Default
#'   \code{FALSE}: with a non-empty \code{na}, \code{fwrite}'s \code{"auto"}
#'   would quote every header and character field, which command-line
#'   breeding programs (HIBLUP, DMU, ...) cannot parse. Use \code{"auto"} if
#'   values may contain the separator.
#' @param ...         Further arguments passed to \code{\link[data.table]{fwrite}}
#'   (e.g. \code{col.names = FALSE} for software that expects no header).
#'
#' @return An invisible \code{character} vector of the files written
#'   (length 0 when nothing was written).
#'
#' @details
#' **Nested column classification (mutually exclusive):**
#' \itemize{
#'   \item \emph{Exportable} — every element inherits from \code{data.frame} or \code{data.table}.
#'   \item \emph{Non-exportable} — empty lists or elements of any other class
#'     (e.g. model objects). Reported to the console; never written.
#' }
#'
#' **Directory layout:**
#' \code{path / <group1_value> / <group2_value> / <nest_col_name>.<file_type>}
#'
#' Group values are sanitised (characters that are invalid in file names,
#' such as slashes, colons or asterisks, become underscores), so they can
#' never create extra directory levels. The
#' grouping columns must identify every row uniquely; otherwise rows would
#' overwrite each other's files and the function stops with an error listing
#' the duplicated targets.
#'
#' **Performance notes:**
#' \itemize{
#'   \item Row data is accessed via \code{.subset2()} (zero-copy column access) rather than
#'     \code{data[i]}, eliminating per-row \code{data.table} allocation in the hot loop.
#'   \item All output directory paths are pre-computed in a single vectorised
#'     \code{do.call(file.path, ...)} call; only the unique directories are created.
#'   \item The field separator and output filenames are computed once before the loop.
#' }
#'
#' @seealso \code{\link[data.table]{fwrite}}
#'
#' @importFrom data.table is.data.table as.data.table fwrite
#' @export
export_nest <- function(data,
                        by        = NULL,
                        cols      = NULL,
                        path      = tempdir(),
                        file_type = "txt",
                        na        = "NA",
                        quote     = FALSE,
                        ...) {
  # Internally the long, explicit names are used for readability.
  nest_dt     <- data
  group_cols  <- by
  nest_cols   <- cols
  export_path <- path

  # -- 1. Validation (fail fast) ------------------------------------------------
  if (!is.data.frame(nest_dt))
    stop("`data` must be a data.frame or data.table.", call. = FALSE)
  if (!data.table::is.data.table(nest_dt))
    nest_dt <- data.table::as.data.table(nest_dt)
  if (nrow(nest_dt) == 0L)
    stop("`data` must not be empty (nrow == 0).", call. = FALSE)
  if (!is.character(export_path) || length(export_path) != 1L || is.na(export_path))
    stop("`path` must be a single non-NA character string.", call. = FALSE)
  if (!is.character(na) || length(na) != 1L || is.na(na))
    stop("`na` must be a single character string, e.g. \"NA\" or \"-9999\".",
         call. = FALSE)
  file_type <- .check_choice(tolower(trimws(file_type)), c("txt", "csv"), "file_type")
  sep  <- if (file_type == "txt") "\t" else ","
  dots <- list(...)
  .check_fwrite_dots(dots, "export_nest")

  # -- 2. Classify list-columns -------------------------------------------------
  .is_df_list_col <- function(x) {
    if (!is.list(x) || length(x) == 0L) return(FALSE)
    all(vapply(x, function(e) is.null(e) || is.data.frame(e), logical(1L))) &&
      any(vapply(x, is.data.frame, logical(1L)))
  }
  all_list_cols <- names(nest_dt)[vapply(nest_dt, is.list, logical(1L))]
  if (length(all_list_cols) == 0L)
    stop("`data` contains no list-columns (nested columns).", call. = FALSE)
  df_nested_cols  <- all_list_cols[vapply(nest_dt[, all_list_cols, with = FALSE],
                                          .is_df_list_col, logical(1L))]
  other_list_cols <- setdiff(all_list_cols, df_nested_cols)

  # -- 3. Resolve nested columns to export -------------------------------------
  if (is.null(nest_cols)) {
    if (length(df_nested_cols) == 0L)
      stop("No data.frame/data.table nested columns found. Specify `cols` ",
           "explicitly or convert list-column elements first.", call. = FALSE)
    nest_cols <- df_nested_cols
    message("[ export_nest ] Auto-selected nested columns: ",
            paste(nest_cols, collapse = ", "))
    if (length(other_list_cols) > 0L)
      message("[ export_nest ] Skipping columns holding custom objects ",
              "(cannot be written as txt/csv): ",
              paste(other_list_cols, collapse = ", "))
  } else {
    if (!is.character(nest_cols) || length(nest_cols) == 0L)
      stop("`cols` must be a non-empty character vector.", call. = FALSE)
    invalid_cols <- setdiff(nest_cols, names(nest_dt))
    if (length(invalid_cols) > 0L)
      stop("Column(s) in `cols` not found in `data`: ",
           paste(invalid_cols, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
    non_df_cols <- setdiff(nest_cols, df_nested_cols)
    if (length(non_df_cols) > 0L) {
      warning("Column(s) not holding data.frame/data.table objects will be skipped: ",
              paste(non_df_cols, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
      nest_cols <- intersect(nest_cols, df_nested_cols)
    }
    if (length(nest_cols) == 0L)
      stop("No valid data.frame/data.table columns remain after filtering.",
           call. = FALSE)
  }

  # -- 4. Resolve grouping columns ----------------------------------------------
  if (is.null(group_cols)) {
    group_cols <- setdiff(names(nest_dt), all_list_cols)
    message("[ export_nest ] ",
            if (length(group_cols)) paste0("Auto-selected grouping columns: ",
                                           paste(group_cols, collapse = ", "))
            else "No grouping columns found; writing to the root export path.")
  } else {
    if (!is.character(group_cols) || length(group_cols) == 0L)
      stop("`by` must be a non-empty character vector (or NULL).", call. = FALSE)
    missing_cols <- setdiff(group_cols, names(nest_dt))
    if (length(missing_cols) > 0L)
      stop("Column(s) in `by` not found in `data`: ",
           paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
    bad_type <- intersect(group_cols, all_list_cols)
    if (length(bad_type) > 0L)
      stop("`by` must not contain list-columns: ",
           paste(bad_type, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }

  # -- 5. Directory paths (vectorised, sanitised) -------------------------------
  # Group values are sanitised so that "/", "..", ":" etc. can never create
  # unexpected directory levels or invalid file names.
  if (length(group_cols) > 0L) {
    segs <- lapply(nest_dt[, group_cols, with = FALSE], .safe_path_segment)
    group_paths <- do.call(file.path, c(list(export_path), unname(segs)))
  } else {
    group_paths <- rep(export_path, nrow(nest_dt))
  }

  # Each row writes <dir>/<nest_col>.<ext>; identical directories would make
  # rows overwrite each other's files, so this is an error, not a silent loss.
  # The comparison is case-insensitive because Windows/macOS file systems are.
  dup <- duplicated(tolower(group_paths))
  if (any(dup))
    stop("`by` (", if (length(group_cols)) paste(group_cols, collapse = ", ")
         else "none", ") do not uniquely identify the rows of `data`, so files ",
         "would overwrite each other. Duplicated target(s):\n  ",
         paste(utils::head(unique(group_paths[dup]), 5L), collapse = "\n  "),
         "\nAdd more columns to `by`.", call. = FALSE)

  for (d in unique(group_paths)) dir.create(d, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  not_created <- unique(group_paths)[!dir.exists(unique(group_paths))]
  if (length(not_created) > 0L)
    stop("Could not create directory/directories:\n  ",
         paste(not_created, collapse = "\n  "), call. = FALSE)

  # -- 6. Write ---------------------------------------------------------------
  filenames <- stats::setNames(paste0(.safe_path_segment(nest_cols), ".", file_type),
                               nest_cols)
  written <- character(0L)

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(nest_dt))) {
    for (col_name in nest_cols) {
      elem <- .subset2(nest_dt, col_name)[[i]]          # zero-copy access
      if (is.null(elem) || nrow(elem) == 0L) next       # nothing to write
      file_path <- file.path(group_paths[i], filenames[[col_name]])
      ok <- tryCatch({
        do.call(data.table::fwrite,
                c(list(x = elem, file = file_path, sep = sep, na = na, quote = quote),
                  dots))
        TRUE
      }, error = function(e) {
        warning(sprintf("[ export_nest ] Failed to export column '%s' at row %d: %s",
                        col_name, i, conditionMessage(e)), call. = FALSE)
        FALSE
      })
      if (ok) written <- c(written, file_path)
    }
  }

  message(sprintf("[ export_nest ] Export complete. %d file(s) written to: %s",
                  length(written), export_path))
  invisible(written)
}
```

```{r example-export_nest}
# Example: Basic nested data export workflow
# A dedicated sub-folder of tempdir() keeps the clean-up safe
out_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "mintyr_export_nest")

# Step 1: Create nested data structure
dt_nest <- w2l_nest(
  data = iris,              # Input iris dataset
  cols = 1:2,               # Columns to be nested
  by = "Species"            # Grouping variable
)

# Step 2: Export nested data to files
files <- export_nest(
  data = dt_nest,                    # Input nested data.table
  cols = "data",                     # Column containing nested data
  by = c("name", "Species"),         # Columns to create directory structure
  path = out_dir
)
# Returns (invisibly) the paths of the written files
# Directory structure: out_dir/<name>/<Species>/data.txt
files

# Clean up
unlink(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```

```{r tests-export_nest}
test_that("export_nest writes one file per row and returns the paths", {
  out <- file.path(tempdir(), "test_export_nest")
  on.exit(unlink(out, recursive = TRUE))
  nd <- w2l_nest(iris, cols = 1:2, by = "Species")
  files <- suppressMessages(export_nest(nd, path = out))
  expect_length(files, 6L)
  expect_true(all(file.exists(files)))
})

test_that("export_nest refuses to overwrite files of other rows", {
  out <- file.path(tempdir(), "test_export_nest_dup")
  on.exit(unlink(out, recursive = TRUE))
  nd <- w2l_nest(iris, cols = 1:2, by = "Species")
  expect_error(suppressMessages(export_nest(nd, by = "Species", path = out)),
               "uniquely identify")
})

test_that("export_nest sanitises group values", {
  out <- file.path(tempdir(), "test_export_nest_safe")
  on.exit(unlink(out, recursive = TRUE))
  nd <- data.table::data.table(g = c("a/b", ".."), data = list(iris[1:2, ], iris[3:4, ]))
  files <- suppressMessages(export_nest(nd, path = out))
  expect_identical(basename(dirname(files)), c("a_b", "unnamed"))
})

test_that("export_nest writes plain, unquoted text with explicit NA", {
  out <- file.path(tempdir(), "test_export_nest_na")
  on.exit(unlink(out, recursive = TRUE))
  nd <- data.table::data.table(g = "x", data = list(data.frame(a = c(1, NA), b = c("u", "v"))))
  f <- suppressMessages(export_nest(nd, path = out))
  expect_identical(readLines(f), c("a\tb", "1\tu", "NA\tv"))
  f <- suppressMessages(export_nest(nd, path = out, na = "-9999", col.names = FALSE))
  expect_identical(readLines(f), c("1\tu", "-9999\tv"))
  expect_error(suppressMessages(export_nest(nd, path = out, sep = ";")), "dedicated")
})
```

# export_list
    
```{r function-export_list}
#' Export a List of Data Frames with Hierarchical Directory Management
#'
#' @description
#' Exports every element of a named (or unnamed) \code{list} of \code{data.frame} /
#' \code{data.table} objects to \code{txt} or \code{csv} files.  Element names may
#' contain forward-slashes (\code{/}) to encode arbitrary subdirectory depth, e.g.
#' \code{"group_a/subject_01/results"} writes
#' \code{<path>/group_a/subject_01/results.txt}.
#' Unnamed elements are automatically labelled \code{split_<i>}.
#'
#' @param data        A non-empty \code{list} whose elements are \code{data.frame},
#'   \code{data.table}, or any object coercible via \code{data.table::as.data.table()}.
#' @param path        Single character string - the root export directory.
#'   Created recursively if absent. Defaults to \code{tempdir()}.
#' @param file_type   \code{"txt"} (tab-separated, default) or \code{"csv"}
#'   (comma-separated). Case-insensitive.
#' @param na          Single string written for missing values. Default \code{"NA"}.
#'   Use e.g. \code{"-9999"} for DMU.
#' @param quote       Passed to \code{\link[data.table]{fwrite}}. Default
#'   \code{FALSE}: with a non-empty \code{na}, \code{fwrite}'s \code{"auto"}
#'   would quote every header and character field, which command-line
#'   breeding programs (HIBLUP, DMU, ...) cannot parse. Use \code{"auto"} if
#'   values may contain the separator.
#' @param ...         Further arguments passed to \code{\link[data.table]{fwrite}}
#'   (e.g. \code{col.names = FALSE}).
#'
#' @return An invisible named \code{character} vector of the file paths
#'   written, with length equal to the number of successfully exported elements.
#'   The total count is accessible via \code{length()} on the return value.
#'
#' @details
#' **Performance design:**
#' \itemize{
#'   \item All element names are resolved and path components split in a single
#'     vectorised pass \emph{before} the write loop, so no string work occurs
#'     inside the hot path.
#'   \item Unique subdirectories are collected and created in one batch
#'     (\code{k} \code{dir.create()} syscalls, where \code{k} \eqn{\le} \code{n}).
#'   \item The field separator is resolved once at function entry.
#'   \item \code{as.data.table()} on an existing \code{data.table} is a
#'     reference-pass (no copy).
#' }
#'
#' **Name handling:** each \code{/}-separated component of an element name is
#' sanitised separately (invalid characters become \code{_}; \code{..} cannot
#' escape \code{path}). If two elements map to the same file
#' (compared case-insensitively), the function stops instead of overwriting.
#'
#' **Error handling:**
#' Individual element failures emit a \code{warning} and are skipped; the
#' remaining elements continue to be processed.
#'
#' @seealso \code{\link[data.table]{fwrite}}
#'
#' @importFrom data.table is.data.table as.data.table fwrite
#' @export
export_list <- function(data,
                        path      = tempdir(),
                        file_type = "txt",
                        na        = "NA",
                        quote     = FALSE,
                        ...) {
  split_dt    <- data
  export_path <- path

  # -- 1. Validation (fail fast) ------------------------------------------------
  # A data.frame is a list too; without this check each column would be
  # written as a separate file.
  if (!is.list(split_dt) || is.data.frame(split_dt))
    stop("`data` must be a list of data.frame / data.table objects ",
         "(wrap a single table in list()).", call. = FALSE)
  if (length(split_dt) == 0L) {
    message("[ export_list ] `data` is empty - nothing to export.")
    return(invisible(character(0L)))
  }
  not_df <- !vapply(split_dt, is.data.frame, logical(1L))
  if (any(not_df))
    stop("All elements of `data` must be data.frames or data.tables. ",
         "Invalid element(s) at index: ", paste(which(not_df), collapse = ", "),
         call. = FALSE)
  if (!is.character(export_path) || length(export_path) != 1L || is.na(export_path))
    stop("`path` must be a single non-NA character string.", call. = FALSE)
  if (!is.character(na) || length(na) != 1L || is.na(na))
    stop("`na` must be a single character string, e.g. \"NA\" or \"-9999\".",
         call. = FALSE)
  file_type <- .check_choice(tolower(trimws(file_type)), c("txt", "csv"), "file_type")
  sep  <- if (file_type == "txt") "\t" else ","
  dots <- list(...)
  .check_fwrite_dots(dots, "export_list")

  # -- 2. Element names -> sanitised relative paths -----------------------------
  n         <- length(split_dt)
  raw_names <- names(split_dt)
  if (is.null(raw_names)) raw_names <- rep("", n)
  raw_names[is.na(raw_names)] <- ""
  elem_names <- ifelse(nzchar(raw_names), raw_names, paste0("split_", seq_len(n)))

  # "/" in a name encodes sub-directories; each component is sanitised on its
  # own, and empty components ("a//b", leading "/") are dropped.
  rel_paths <- vapply(strsplit(elem_names, "/", fixed = TRUE), function(p) {
    p <- p[nzchar(p)]
    if (length(p) == 0L) p <- "unnamed"
    paste(.safe_path_segment(p), collapse = "/")
  }, character(1L))
  full_paths <- file.path(export_path, paste0(rel_paths, ".", file_type))

  dup <- duplicated(tolower(full_paths))
  if (any(dup))
    stop("Several list elements map to the same output file and would ",
         "overwrite each other:\n  ",
         paste(utils::head(unique(full_paths[dup]), 5L), collapse = "\n  "),
         "\nMake the list names unique.", call. = FALSE)

  # -- 3. Directories (one call per unique directory) ---------------------------
  all_dirs <- unique(c(export_path, dirname(full_paths)))
  for (d in all_dirs) dir.create(d, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  not_created <- all_dirs[!dir.exists(all_dirs)]
  if (length(not_created) > 0L)
    stop("Could not create directory/directories:\n  ",
         paste(not_created, collapse = "\n  "), call. = FALSE)

  # -- 4. Write ---------------------------------------------------------------
  written <- rep(FALSE, n)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    elem <- split_dt[[i]]
    if (nrow(elem) == 0L) next                         # nothing to write
    written[i] <- tryCatch({
      do.call(data.table::fwrite,
              c(list(x = elem, file = full_paths[i], sep = sep, na = na, quote = quote),
                dots))
      TRUE
    }, error = function(e) {
      warning(sprintf("[ export_list ] Failed to export element %d ('%s'): %s",
                      i, elem_names[i], conditionMessage(e)), call. = FALSE)
      FALSE
    })
  }

  out <- stats::setNames(full_paths[written], elem_names[written])
  message(sprintf("[ export_list ] Export complete. %d / %d file(s) written to: %s",
                  sum(written), n, export_path))
  invisible(out)
}
```
  
```{r example-export_list}
# Example: Export split data to files
out_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "mintyr_export_list")

# Step 1: Create split data structure
dt_split <- w2l_split(
  data = iris,              # Input iris dataset
  cols = 1:2,               # Columns to be split
  by = "Species"            # Grouping variable
)

# Step 2: Export split data to files
files <- export_list(
  data = dt_split,          # Input list of data.tables
  path = out_dir
)
# Returns (invisibly) a named vector of the written file paths
files

# Clean up
unlink(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```

```{r tests-export_list}
test_that("export_list writes named files and sub-directories", {
  out <- file.path(tempdir(), "test_export_list")
  on.exit(unlink(out, recursive = TRUE))
  files <- suppressMessages(export_list(list("g1/a" = iris, b = mtcars), path = out))
  expect_identical(names(files), c("g1/a", "b"))
  expect_identical(files[["g1/a"]], file.path(out, "g1", "a.txt"))
  expect_true(all(file.exists(files)))
})

test_that("export_list rejects a data.frame and duplicated targets", {
  out <- file.path(tempdir(), "test_export_list_err")
  on.exit(unlink(out, recursive = TRUE))
  expect_error(export_list(iris, path = out), "list of")
  expect_error(suppressMessages(export_list(list(a = iris, A = iris), path = out)),
               "same output file")
})

test_that("export_list cannot escape the export directory", {
  out <- file.path(tempdir(), "test_export_list_safe")
  on.exit(unlink(out, recursive = TRUE))
  f <- suppressMessages(export_list(list("../x" = iris), path = out))
  expect_identical(f[[1]], file.path(out, "unnamed", "x.txt"))
})
```

# import_csv

```{r function-import_csv}
#' Flexible CSV/TXT File Import via data.table
#'
#' @description
#' Reads one or more CSV/TXT files using \code{\link[data.table]{fread}} as the backend.
#' Supports flexible combination strategies and source-file tracking. All return values
#' are \code{data.table} objects.
#'
#' @param file A non-empty \code{character} vector of file paths to CSV/TXT files.
#'   All paths must point to existing, accessible files.
#' @param combine A \code{logical} scalar controlling the combination strategy:
#'   \itemize{
#'     \item \code{TRUE} (default): Combine all files into a single \code{data.table}.
#'     \item \code{FALSE}: Return a named \code{list} of individual \code{data.table} objects.
#'   }
#' @param file_col A \code{character} scalar or \code{NULL} specifying the source-tracking
#'   column name (default: \code{"_file"}). Set to \code{NULL} to suppress the source column.
#'   Only applies when \code{combine = TRUE}.
#' @param full_path A \code{logical} scalar controlling path representation in labels:
#'   \itemize{
#'     \item \code{FALSE} (default): Use only the filename (via \code{basename()}).
#'     \item \code{TRUE}: Use the full file path.
#'   }
#' @param keep_ext A \code{logical} scalar controlling whether the file extension is
#'   retained in labels:
#'   \itemize{
#'     \item \code{FALSE} (default): Strip the file extension (e.g., \code{"data"}).
#'     \item \code{TRUE}: Retain the file extension (e.g., \code{"data.csv"}).
#'   }
#' @param ... Additional arguments passed directly to \code{\link[data.table]{fread}}
#'   (e.g., \code{select}, \code{drop}, \code{na.strings}, \code{skip}, \code{nThread}).
#'
#' @details
#' Label generation is controlled by the combination of \code{full_path} and \code{keep_ext}:
#' \tabular{ll}{
#'   \code{full_path = FALSE, keep_ext = FALSE} \tab Filename without extension: \code{"data"} \cr
#'   \code{full_path = FALSE, keep_ext = TRUE}  \tab Filename with extension: \code{"data.csv"} \cr
#'   \code{full_path = TRUE,  keep_ext = FALSE} \tab Full path without extension: \code{"/path/to/data"} \cr
#'   \code{full_path = TRUE,  keep_ext = TRUE}  \tab Full path with extension: \code{"/path/to/data.csv"} \cr
#' }
#'
#' When \code{combine = TRUE} and \code{file_col} is not \code{NULL},
#' \code{\link[data.table]{rbindlist}} is called with \code{idcol = file_col},
#' which generates the source column directly during the merge step without any
#' intermediate copies.
#'
#' @return
#' \itemize{
#'   \item \code{combine = TRUE}: A single \code{data.table} containing all imported rows.
#'     If \code{file_col} is not \code{NULL}, the first column contains the source
#'     file label for each row.
#'   \item \code{combine = FALSE}: A named \code{list} of \code{data.table} objects.
#'     List names are derived from file paths according to \code{full_path} and
#'     \code{keep_ext} settings.
#' }
#'
#' @note
#' \itemize{
#'   \item All specified files must exist and be readable at call time.
#'   \item \code{combine = TRUE} assumes compatible column structures across files;
#'     mismatched columns are automatically aligned via \code{fill = TRUE}.
#'   \item Logical parameters (\code{combine}, \code{full_path}, \code{keep_ext}) reject
#'     \code{NA} values explicitly.
#'   \item Only the extension of the file itself is stripped; dots in directory
#'     names (e.g. \code{"v1.2/file"}) are left intact.
#'   \item Duplicated labels (same file name in different folders) trigger a
#'     warning and are made unique with \code{make.unique()}.
#' }
#'
#' @seealso
#' \code{\link[data.table]{fread}}, \code{\link[data.table]{rbindlist}}
#'
#' @import data.table
#' @export
import_csv <- function(file,
                       combine   = TRUE,
                       file_col  = "_file",
                       full_path = FALSE,
                       keep_ext  = FALSE,
                       ...) {

  # -- 1. Input validation ----------------------------------------------------
  if (!is.character(file) || length(file) == 0L || anyNA(file))
    stop("`file` must be a non-empty character vector without NA.", call. = FALSE)
  missing_files <- file[!file.exists(file)]
  if (length(missing_files) > 0L)
    stop("The following files do not exist or cannot be accessed:\n",
         paste0("  - ", missing_files, collapse = "\n"), call. = FALSE)
  .check_flag(combine, "combine")
  .check_flag(full_path, "full_path")
  .check_flag(keep_ext, "keep_ext")
  if (!is.null(file_col) &&
      (!is.character(file_col) || length(file_col) != 1L ||
       is.na(file_col) || !nzchar(file_col)))
    stop("`file_col` must be a single non-empty character string, or NULL.",
         call. = FALSE)

  # -- 2. Labels --------------------------------------------------------------
  # .strip_ext() only touches the last path component, so dots in directory
  # names (e.g. "v1.2/file") are never mistaken for an extension.
  labels <- if (full_path) file else basename(file)
  if (!keep_ext) labels <- .strip_ext(labels)

  if (anyDuplicated(labels)) {
    dup <- unique(labels[duplicated(labels)])
    warning("Duplicated source label(s): ", paste(dup, collapse = ", "),
            ". Files with the same name in different folders cannot be told apart; ",
            "labels were made unique with make.unique(). ",
            "Consider `full_path = TRUE`.", call. = FALSE)
    labels <- make.unique(labels, sep = "_")
  }

  # -- 3. Read ----------------------------------------------------------------
  file_list        <- lapply(file, data.table::fread, ...)
  names(file_list) <- labels

  if (!combine) return(file_list)

  data.table::rbindlist(file_list, use.names = TRUE, fill = TRUE,
                        idcol = file_col)
}
```

```{r examples-import_csv}
# Example: CSV file import demonstrations

# Setup test files
csv_files <- mintyr_example(
  mintyr_examples("csv_test")     # Get example CSV files
)

# Example 1: Import and combine CSV files using data.table
import_csv(
  csv_files,                      # Input CSV file paths
  combine = TRUE,                 # Combine all files into one data.table
  file_col = "_file",             # Column name for file source
  keep_ext = TRUE,                # Include .csv extension in _file column
  full_path = TRUE                # Show complete file paths in _file column
)
```

```{r tests-import_csv}
test_that("import_csv keeps dots in directory names", {
  d <- file.path(tempdir(), "v1.2")
  dir.create(d, showWarnings = FALSE)
  on.exit(unlink(d, recursive = TRUE))
  f <- file.path(d, c("noext", "data.csv"))
  data.table::fwrite(data.frame(a = 1), f[1])
  data.table::fwrite(data.frame(a = 2), f[2])
  res <- import_csv(f, full_path = TRUE)
  expect_identical(unique(res[["_file"]]), c(f[1], file.path(d, "data")))
})

test_that("import_csv warns about duplicated labels and supports combine = FALSE", {
  d1 <- file.path(tempdir(), "csv_a"); d2 <- file.path(tempdir(), "csv_b")
  dir.create(d1, showWarnings = FALSE); dir.create(d2, showWarnings = FALSE)
  on.exit(unlink(c(d1, d2), recursive = TRUE))
  f <- c(file.path(d1, "x.csv"), file.path(d2, "x.csv"))
  for (p in f) data.table::fwrite(data.frame(a = 1), p)
  expect_warning(res <- import_csv(f, combine = FALSE), "Duplicated")
  expect_identical(names(res), c("x", "x_1"))
})
```

# import_xlsx
    
```{r function-import_xlsx}
#' Import Data from XLSX Files
#'
#' @description
#' A high-performance function for importing data from one or multiple Excel
#' files into \code{data.table} format, with fine-grained control over source
#' tracking columns, sheet selection, row skipping, multi-row headers, and
#' optional parallel reading across (file, sheet) pairs.
#'
#' Performance characteristics:
#' \itemize{
#'   \item \code{excel_sheets()} called exactly once per file (cached).
#'   \item The real cost of an Excel import is \code{read_excel()} parsing,
#'         which is single-threaded C++ and \emph{not} affected by the
#'         \code{data.table} thread pool. The flat (file x sheet) task list is
#'         therefore read in parallel \strong{across processes} when
#'         \code{workers > 1}: a fork pool on Unix/macOS, a PSOCK cluster on
#'         Windows. The cluster / fork pool is always torn down on exit.
#'   \item \code{setDT()} converts tibbles in-place — zero vector copies.
#'   \item Tracking columns injected via \code{:=} on small per-sheet tables
#'         \emph{before} the single final \code{rbindlist}.
#'   \item The final \code{rbindlist} uses the ambient \code{data.table} thread
#'         pool; tune it globally with \code{\link[data.table]{setDTthreads}} if
#'         needed. Workers are pinned to a single thread during the read phase
#'         so parallel processes do not oversubscribe cores.
#' }
#'
#' @param file       Non-empty \code{character} vector of paths to existing
#'                   \code{.xlsx} / \code{.xls} files.
#' @param combine    \code{logical(1)}. \code{TRUE} (default) binds all sheets
#'                   into a single \code{data.table}. \code{FALSE} returns a
#'                   flat named list keyed as \code{"<filename>_<sheetname>"}.
#' @param sheet      Positive \code{integer} vector, \code{character} vector of
#'                   sheet names, or \code{NULL} (default, every sheet).
#'                   Indices / names must exist in all supplied files.
#' @param skip       Non-negative \code{integer(1)}. Number of rows to skip
#'                   before the header (e.g. a title row). Default \code{0L}.
#' @param header_rows Positive \code{integer(1)}. Number of header rows below
#'                   the skipped rows. Default \code{1L} (ordinary sheets).
#'                   Values \code{> 1} combine the rows into one name per
#'                   column (see Details); data start on the next row.
#' @param header_sep \code{character(1)}. Separator used to join the levels of
#'                   a multi-row header. Default \code{"_"}.
#' @param header_fill How merged header cells are resolved when
#'                   \code{header_rows > 1}: \code{"auto"} (default) reads the
#'                   merged ranges stored in \code{.xlsx}/\code{.xlsm} files and
#'                   falls back to \code{"right"} for \code{.xls};
#'                   \code{"right"} fills upper levels to the right (heuristic,
#'                   no merge information needed); \code{"none"} uses the
#'                   cells as they are.
#' @param file_col   \code{character(1)} or \code{NULL}. Name of the column
#'                   recording the source file (extension stripped) when
#'                   \code{combine = TRUE}. Default \code{"excel_name"};
#'                   \code{NULL} omits the column. Ignored when
#'                   \code{combine = FALSE} (provenance is in the list names).
#' @param sheet_col  \code{character(1)} or \code{NULL}. Name of the column
#'                   recording the source sheet when \code{combine = TRUE}.
#'                   Default \code{"sheet_name"}; \code{NULL} omits it.
#'                   The defaults match \code{export_xlsx()}, so the result
#'                   can be written back to the original layout.
#' @param workers    \code{integer(1)}. Number of parallel processes used to
#'                   read the (file x sheet) tasks. Default \code{1L} (serial).
#'                   Values \code{> 1} open a fork pool on Unix/macOS or a
#'                   PSOCK cluster on Windows; the pool is capped at the number
#'                   of tasks and always shut down on exit. Parallel reading
#'                   pays off when files are large or numerous; for many tiny
#'                   sheets the process / serialization overhead can dominate,
#'                   so leave this at \code{1L} unless the import is heavy.
#' @param verbose    \code{logical(1)}. When \code{TRUE}, print one
#'                   \code{message()} per sheet (source file, sheet name, and
#'                   row x col dimensions, with empty sheets flagged) followed
#'                   by a summary line. Default \code{FALSE}. Output is emitted
#'                   from the master process, so it surfaces identically in
#'                   serial and parallel modes.
#' @param on_error   \code{"stop"} (default) or \code{"warn"}. With
#'                   \code{"stop"}, any file or sheet that cannot be read
#'                   aborts the import with one error listing \emph{all}
#'                   failures. With \code{"warn"}, failed files/sheets are
#'                   skipped and listed in a single warning; the import only
#'                   fails when nothing could be read.
#' @param ...        Additional arguments forwarded to
#'                   \code{\link[readxl]{read_excel}} (e.g. \code{col_types},
#'                   \code{na}, \code{trim_ws}). \strong{Do not} pass
#'                   \code{path}, \code{sheet}, or \code{skip} here; use the
#'                   dedicated parameters above. With \code{header_rows > 1},
#'                   \code{col_names} and \code{range} are set internally and
#'                   must not be passed either; \code{col_types} then refers
#'                   to the data columns.
#'
#' @details
#' \strong{Multi-row headers.} Many hand-made workbooks have a title row and
#' a header spread over several rows with merged cells, e.g.
#' \preformatted{
#' row 1  Growth test records
#' row 2  ID | Breed | Weight (kg)   | Backfat (mm)
#' row 3     |       | Start | End   | P2 | Loin
#' row 4  A001 | Duroc | 28.5 | 102.3 | 11.2 | 56.1
#' }
#' \code{import_xlsx(f, skip = 1, header_rows = 2)} returns the columns
#' \code{ID}, \code{Breed}, \code{Weight (kg)_Start}, \code{Weight (kg)_End},
#' \code{Backfat (mm)_P2}, \code{Backfat (mm)_Loin}. The rules are:
#' \itemize{
#'   \item Merged cells only store their value in their top-left cell. With
#'     \code{header_fill = "auto"} the merged ranges are read from the
#'     workbook itself (\code{<mergeCell>} entries of the sheet XML), and each
#'     range is filled with its value, horizontally and vertically. Header
#'     cells that are genuinely empty stay empty, so a column whose upper
#'     cell is blank gets only its lower label.
#'   \item Without merge information (\code{.xls} files, or
#'     \code{header_fill = "right"}), every level except the last is filled to
#'     the right, restarting wherever a higher level starts a new label.
#'   \item Per column, empty parts and repeated parts (vertically merged
#'     cells) are dropped and the remaining parts joined with
#'     \code{header_sep}; line breaks inside a cell become spaces.
#'   \item Columns without any header become \code{col_<j>}; duplicates are
#'     made unique.
#'   \item The header block is read as text, but the data block is read
#'     separately, so numbers and dates keep their types (reading the whole
#'     sheet as text would turn dates into serial numbers such as
#'     \code{"45296"}).
#'   \item Completely empty data rows (spacer or trailing rows) are dropped.
#' }
#' Labels that are only \emph{visually} spread over several columns with
#' "Center Across Selection" (instead of real merging) are not merges; use
#' \code{header_fill = "right"} for such sheets. Reading the merge
#' information re-scans the sheet XML once, which costs a fraction of the
#' import time and only happens when \code{header_rows > 1}.
#'
#' @return
#' \describe{
#'   \item{\code{combine = TRUE}}{A \code{data.table}. Tracking columns
#'     \code{excel_name} and/or \code{sheet_name} are prepended when their
#'     respective \code{file_col} / \code{sheet_col} are not \code{NULL}.}
#'   \item{\code{combine = FALSE}}{A named \code{list} of \code{data.table}s,
#'     each element named \code{"<filename>_<sheetname>"}. The list carries a
#'     \code{"source_files"} attribute with the original file paths.}
#' }
#'
#' @note
#' Files that share the same base name in different folders cannot be told
#' apart by \code{file_col}; a warning is issued and the labels are made
#' unique, so a later \code{export_xlsx()} round trip does not merge them.
#'
#' @importFrom data.table setDT setcolorder setattr setalloccol getDTthreads
#'   setDTthreads rbindlist `:=`
#' @importFrom readxl read_excel excel_sheets cell_limits
#' @importFrom parallel makeCluster stopCluster parLapply clusterEvalQ mclapply
#' @export
import_xlsx <- function(file,
                        combine   = TRUE,
                        sheet     = NULL,
                        skip      = 0L,
                        header_rows = 1L,
                        header_sep  = "_",
                        header_fill = "auto",
                        file_col  = "excel_name",
                        sheet_col = "sheet_name",
                        workers   = 1L,
                        verbose   = FALSE,
                        on_error  = "stop",
                        ...) {

  # -- 0. Tracking-column arguments ------------------------------------------
  for (nm in c("file_col", "sheet_col")) {
    val <- get(nm)
    if (!is.null(val) && (!is.character(val) || length(val) != 1L || is.na(val) ||
                          !nzchar(val)))
      stop(sprintf("`%s` must be a single non-empty string, or NULL.", nm), call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!is.null(file_col) && identical(file_col, sheet_col))
    stop("`file_col` and `sheet_col` must differ.", call. = FALSE)

  # -- 1. Input validation ----------------------------------------------------
  if (!is.character(file) || length(file) == 0L || anyNA(file))
    stop("`file` must be a non-empty character vector without NA.", call. = FALSE)
  bad <- file[!file.exists(file)]
  if (length(bad))
    stop("File(s) not found:\n  ", paste(bad, collapse = "\n  "), call. = FALSE)
  .check_flag(combine, "combine")
  if (!is.null(sheet)) {
    if (is.character(sheet)) {
      if (length(sheet) == 0L || anyNA(sheet) || any(!nzchar(sheet)))
        stop("`sheet` names must be non-empty strings.", call. = FALSE)
    } else if (!is.numeric(sheet) || length(sheet) == 0L || anyNA(sheet) ||
               any(sheet < 1) || any(sheet != floor(sheet))) {
      stop("`sheet` must be a positive integer vector, a character vector of ",
           "sheet names, or NULL.", call. = FALSE)
    } else {
      sheet <- as.integer(sheet)
    }
  }
  skip        <- .check_count(skip, "skip", 0L)
  header_rows <- .check_count(header_rows, "header_rows", 1L)
  if (!is.character(header_sep) || length(header_sep) != 1L || is.na(header_sep))
    stop("`header_sep` must be a single character string.", call. = FALSE)
  .check_choice(header_fill, c("auto", "right", "none"), "header_fill")
  .check_choice(on_error, c("stop", "warn"), "on_error")
  .check_flag(verbose, "verbose")
  workers <- .check_count(workers, "workers", 1L)

  dots     <- list(...)
  reserved <- intersect(names(dots), c("path", "sheet", "skip",
                                       if (header_rows > 1L) c("col_names", "range")))
  if (length(reserved))
    stop(sprintf("Do not pass %s via `...`; use the dedicated parameter(s) instead.",
                 paste0("`", reserved, "`", collapse = ", ")), call. = FALSE)

  # -- 2. Restore the data.table thread pool on exit ---------------------------
  old_threads <- data.table::getDTthreads()
  on.exit(data.table::setDTthreads(old_threads), add = TRUE)

  # -- 3. Source labels -------------------------------------------------------
  file_base <- .strip_ext(basename(file))
  if (anyDuplicated(file_base) && (!is.null(file_col) || !combine)) {
    dup <- unique(file_base[duplicated(file_base)])
    warning("Several files share the same base name (", paste(dup, collapse = ", "),
            "). Their rows cannot be told apart by `file_col`, and ",
            "export_xlsx() would merge them into one workbook. Labels were made ",
            "unique with make.unique().", call. = FALSE)
    file_base <- make.unique(file_base, sep = "_")
  }

  # -- 4. Sheet directories: one open per file --------------------------------
  # Files that cannot be opened at all are handled like failed sheets.
  sheets_cache <- lapply(file, function(f) tryCatch(readxl::excel_sheets(f),
    error = function(e) structure(list(message = conditionMessage(e)),
                                  class = "mintyr_read_error")))
  open_failed <- vapply(sheets_cache, inherits, logical(1L), what = "mintyr_read_error")
  file_errors <- vapply(which(open_failed), function(i)
    sprintf("  - %s: %s", file[[i]], sheets_cache[[i]]$message), character(1L))
  if (any(open_failed) && (on_error == "stop" || all(open_failed)))
    stop(sprintf("Failed to open %d of %d file(s):\n", sum(open_failed), length(file)),
         paste(file_errors, collapse = "\n"), call. = FALSE)
  ok_files <- which(!open_failed)

  if (is.numeric(sheet)) {
    min_n <- min(lengths(sheets_cache[ok_files]))
    if (max(sheet) > min_n)
      stop(sprintf("Sheet index %d exceeds the minimum sheet count (%d) across files.",
                   max(sheet), min_n), call. = FALSE)
  } else if (is.character(sheet)) {
    absent <- unlist(lapply(ok_files, function(i) {
      miss <- setdiff(sheet, sheets_cache[[i]])
      if (length(miss)) sprintf("%s: %s", basename(file[[i]]), paste(miss, collapse = ", "))
    }))
    if (length(absent))
      stop("Sheet(s) not found:\n  ", paste(absent, collapse = "\n  "), call. = FALSE)
  }

  # -- 5. Flat (file, sheet) task list ----------------------------------------
  tasks <- unlist(lapply(ok_files, function(i) {
    avail <- sheets_cache[[i]]
    sel   <- if (is.null(sheet)) avail else if (is.character(sheet)) sheet else avail[sheet]
    lapply(sel, function(sht) list(path = file[[i]], base = file_base[[i]], sheet = sht))
  }), recursive = FALSE)

  # -- 6. Read every task (serial or parallel) ---------------------------------
  need_excel <- combine && !is.null(file_col)
  need_sheet <- combine && !is.null(sheet_col)

  read_body <- function(tk) {
    if (header_rows == 1L) {
      raw <- do.call(readxl::read_excel,
                     c(list(path = tk$path, sheet = tk$sheet, skip = skip), dots))
      dt  <- data.table::setDT(raw)
    } else {
      # Multi-row header: the header block is read as text, the data block
      # separately so that readxl still guesses numeric / date types. Both
      # ranges start at column A, which keeps them aligned.
      hdr <- readxl::read_excel(
        tk$path, sheet = tk$sheet, col_names = FALSE, col_types = "text",
        range = readxl::cell_limits(c(skip + 1L, 1L), c(skip + header_rows, NA)),
        .name_repair = "minimal")
      raw <- do.call(readxl::read_excel, c(list(
        path = tk$path, sheet = tk$sheet, col_names = FALSE,
        range = readxl::cell_limits(c(skip + header_rows + 1L, 1L), c(NA, NA)),
        .name_repair = "minimal"), dots))
      # Merged ranges are taken from the workbook itself when possible
      # (.xlsx / .xlsm); .xls files, or a workbook whose XML cannot be
      # parsed, fall back to the right-fill heuristic.
      merges <- NULL
      if (header_fill == "auto" && grepl("\\.xls[xm]$", tk$path, ignore.case = TRUE))
        merges <- tryCatch(xlsx_merges(tk$path, tk$sheet), error = function(e) NULL)
      fill <- if (header_fill == "none") "none" else "right"
      nm <- combine_headers(hdr, header_sep, fill = fill, merges = merges,
                            first_row = skip + 1L)
      dt <- data.table::setDT(raw)
      n  <- ncol(dt)
      if (n == 0L) {
        dt <- data.table::setDT(stats::setNames(rep(list(logical(0L)), length(nm)), nm))
      } else {
        if (length(nm) < n) nm <- make.unique(c(nm, paste0("col_", seq.int(length(nm) + 1L, n))),
                                              sep = header_sep)
        data.table::setnames(dt, nm[seq_len(n)])
        # Rows that are completely empty (spacer rows, trailing blanks) are dropped.
        keep <- Reduce(`|`, lapply(dt, function(x) !is.na(x)))
        if (!all(keep)) dt <- dt[keep]
      }
    }
    if (need_excel) data.table::set(dt, j = file_col,  value = rep(tk$base,  nrow(dt)))
    if (need_sheet) data.table::set(dt, j = sheet_col, value = rep(tk$sheet, nrow(dt)))
    dt
  }
  # Errors are returned as objects instead of thrown, so one bad sheet never
  # aborts a (parallel) batch; they are reported together afterwards.
  read_one <- function(tk) {
    tryCatch(read_body(tk), error = function(e)
      structure(list(message = conditionMessage(e)), class = "mintyr_read_error"))
  }
  # Pure base R helpers, safe to ship to PSOCK workers.
  combine_headers <- .combine_headers
  xlsx_merges     <- .xlsx_merges
  environment(combine_headers) <- environment(xlsx_merges) <- baseenv()
  # Detach read_one from the (large) call frame so PSOCK workers only
  # serialise the few small objects it needs.
  shared <- list2env(
    list(skip = skip, dots = dots, header_rows = header_rows, header_sep = header_sep,
         need_excel = need_excel, need_sheet = need_sheet,
         file_col = file_col, sheet_col = sheet_col,
         header_fill = header_fill, combine_headers = combine_headers,
         xlsx_merges = xlsx_merges),
    parent = globalenv()
  )
  environment(read_body) <- shared
  assign("read_body", read_body, envir = shared)
  environment(read_one) <- shared

  n_tasks     <- length(tasks)
  use_workers <- min(workers, n_tasks)

  if (use_workers > 1L) {
    if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") {
      cl <- parallel::makeCluster(use_workers)
      on.exit(parallel::stopCluster(cl), add = TRUE)
      parallel::clusterEvalQ(cl, data.table::setDTthreads(1L))
      sheet_tables <- parallel::parLapply(cl, tasks, read_one)
    } else {
      data.table::setDTthreads(1L)          # forked children inherit this
      sheet_tables <- parallel::mclapply(tasks, read_one, mc.cores = use_workers)
      # A killed worker (e.g. out of memory) returns NULL or a try-error.
      sheet_tables <- lapply(sheet_tables, function(x) {
        if (is.data.frame(x) || inherits(x, "mintyr_read_error")) x
        else structure(list(message = if (inherits(x, "try-error")) as.character(x)
                            else "worker returned no result (possibly killed, e.g. out of memory)"),
                       class = "mintyr_read_error")
      })
    }
    # Tables serialised back from workers lose their self-reference.
    # setalloccol() returns the repaired table; it must be re-assigned because
    # its argument here is not a plain symbol.
    if (!combine) sheet_tables <- lapply(sheet_tables, data.table::setalloccol)
  } else {
    sheet_tables <- lapply(tasks, read_one)
  }

  # -- 6b. Failures -------------------------------------------------------------
  failed <- vapply(sheet_tables, inherits, logical(1L), what = "mintyr_read_error")
  if (any(failed) || length(file_errors)) {
    info <- c(file_errors, vapply(which(failed), function(i)
      sprintf("  - %s [sheet '%s']: %s", tasks[[i]]$path, tasks[[i]]$sheet,
              sheet_tables[[i]]$message), character(1L)))
    head_msg <- sprintf("Failed to read %d file(s) / %d of %d sheet(s):\n",
                        length(file_errors), sum(failed), length(failed))
    if (on_error == "stop" || all(failed))
      stop(head_msg, paste(info, collapse = "\n"),
           if (on_error == "warn") "\nNothing could be read.", call. = FALSE)
    warning(head_msg, paste(info, collapse = "\n"), "\nThese were skipped.",
            call. = FALSE)
    sheet_tables <- sheet_tables[!failed]
    tasks        <- tasks[!failed]
  }
  n_tasks <- length(tasks)

  if (verbose) {
    dims <- vapply(sheet_tables, function(d) c(nrow(d), ncol(d)), integer(2L))
    for (i in seq_along(sheet_tables))
      message(sprintf("[%d/%d] '%s' / sheet '%s': %d rows x %d cols%s",
                      i, n_tasks, basename(tasks[[i]]$path), tasks[[i]]$sheet,
                      dims[1L, i], dims[2L, i],
                      if (dims[1L, i] == 0L) "  (empty)" else ""))
    message(sprintf("Imported %d sheet(s) from %d file(s); %d total rows.",
                    n_tasks, length(file), sum(dims[1L, ])))
  }

  # -- 7. Assemble ------------------------------------------------------------
  if (combine) {
    data.table::setDTthreads(old_threads)
    out <- data.table::rbindlist(sheet_tables, use.names = TRUE, fill = TRUE)
    front_cols <- c(if (need_excel) file_col, if (need_sheet) sheet_col)
    front_cols <- intersect(front_cols, names(out))
    if (length(front_cols)) data.table::setcolorder(out, front_cols)
    return(out[])
  }

  nms <- vapply(tasks, function(tk) paste(tk$base, tk$sheet, sep = "_"), character(1L))
  out <- stats::setNames(sheet_tables, make.unique(nms, sep = "_"))
  data.table::setattr(out, "source_files", file)
  out
}
```
  
```{r example-import_xlsx}
# Example: Excel file import demonstrations

# Setup test files
xlsx_files <- mintyr_example(
  mintyr_examples("xlsx_test")    # Get example Excel files
)

# Example 1: Import and combine all sheets from all files
import_xlsx(
  xlsx_files,                     # Input Excel file paths
  combine = TRUE                  # Combine all sheets into one data.table
)

# Example 2: Import specific sheets separately
import_xlsx(
  xlsx_files,                     # Input Excel file paths
  combine = FALSE,                 # Keep sheets as separate data.tables
  sheet = 2                       # Only import the second sheet
)

# Example 3: Multi-row header with merged cells and a title row
# (row 1 = title, rows 2-3 = header, data from row 4)
mh_file <- mintyr_example("multiheader_test.xlsx")
import_xlsx(
  mh_file,
  skip = 1,                       # Skip the title row
  header_rows = 2                 # Combine two header rows into one name
)
# The last column has an empty, unmerged upper cell: it is named "Note".
# The heuristic fill would wrongly call it "Backfat (mm)_Note":
names(import_xlsx(mh_file, sheet = 1, skip = 1, header_rows = 2,
                  header_fill = "right"))

# Example 4: Batch import that skips unreadable files instead of stopping
bad_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
writeLines("not a workbook", bad_file)
res <- suppressWarnings(
  import_xlsx(c(mh_file, bad_file), skip = 1, header_rows = 2, on_error = "warn")
)
unique(res$excel_name)
unlink(bad_file)
```

```{r tests-import_xlsx}
make_xlsx <- function() {
  d1 <- file.path(tempdir(), "xl_a"); d2 <- file.path(tempdir(), "xl_b")
  dir.create(d1, showWarnings = FALSE); dir.create(d2, showWarnings = FALSE)
  f <- c(file.path(d1, "2024.xlsx"), file.path(d2, "2024.xlsx"))
  writexl::write_xlsx(list(s1 = data.frame(v = 1:2), s2 = data.frame(v = 3)), f[1])
  writexl::write_xlsx(list(s1 = data.frame(v = 9)), f[2])
  f
}

test_that("import_xlsx adds tracking columns and separates equal base names", {
  f <- make_xlsx(); on.exit(unlink(dirname(f), recursive = TRUE))
  expect_warning(res <- import_xlsx(f), "same base name")
  expect_identical(names(res), c("excel_name", "sheet_name", "v"))
  expect_identical(unique(res$excel_name), c("2024", "2024_1"))
})

test_that("import_xlsx supports custom / omitted tracking columns", {
  f <- make_xlsx()[1]; on.exit(unlink(dirname(f), recursive = TRUE))
  res <- import_xlsx(f, file_col = NULL, sheet_col = "tab")
  expect_identical(names(res), c("tab", "v"))
})

test_that("import_xlsx reads empty sheets", {
  f <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx"); on.exit(unlink(f))
  writexl::write_xlsx(list(e = data.frame()), f)
  expect_equal(nrow(import_xlsx(f)), 0L)
})

test_that("import_xlsx parallel results are safe to modify by reference", {
  skip_on_cran()
  f <- make_xlsx(); on.exit(unlink(dirname(f), recursive = TRUE))
  res <- suppressWarnings(import_xlsx(f, combine = FALSE, workers = 2))
  expect_identical(names(res), c("2024_s1", "2024_s2", "2024_1_s1"))
  expect_silent(res[[1]][, z := 1])
  expect_true("z" %in% names(res[[1]]))
})

test_that(".combine_headers fills merged cells within their parent block", {
  h <- data.frame(a = c("ID", NA), b = c("Weight", "Start"), c = c(NA, "End"),
                  d = c("Backfat", "P2"), e = c(NA, "Loin"), f = c("Note\nfree", NA),
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  expect_identical(.combine_headers(h),
                   c("ID", "Weight_Start", "Weight_End", "Backfat_P2", "Backfat_Loin",
                     "Note free"))
  h3 <- data.frame(a = c("W", "D0", "kg"), b = c(NA, NA, "lb"), c = c(NA, "D21", "kg"),
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  expect_identical(.combine_headers(h3, sep = "."), c("W.D0.kg", "W.D0.lb", "W.D21.kg"))
  expect_identical(.combine_headers(data.frame(a = c(NA, NA), b = c("x", "x"))),
                   c("col_1", "x"))
})

test_that("import_xlsx reads multi-row headers and keeps column types", {
  f <- mintyr_example("multiheader_test.xlsx")
  res <- import_xlsx(f, skip = 1, header_rows = 2)
  expect_identical(names(res),
                   c("excel_name", "sheet_name", "ID", "Breed", "Birth date",
                     "Weight (kg)_Start", "Weight (kg)_End",
                     "Backfat (mm)_P2", "Backfat (mm)_Loin", "Note"))
  expect_equal(nrow(res), 7L)                          # blank spacer rows dropped
  expect_false(anyNA(res$ID))
  expect_type(res[["Weight (kg)_End"]], "double")
  expect_s3_class(res[["Birth date"]], "POSIXct")      # not "45296"
  one <- import_xlsx(f, sheet = "farm_B", skip = 1, header_rows = 2,
                     header_sep = ".", file_col = NULL, sheet_col = NULL)
  expect_identical(names(one)[4], "Weight (kg).Start")
  expect_equal(nrow(one), 3L)
})

test_that(".xlsx_merges reads merged ranges from the workbook", {
  f <- mintyr_example("multiheader_test.xlsx")
  m <- .xlsx_merges(f, "farm_B")
  expect_identical(colnames(m), c("r1", "c1", "r2", "c2"))
  expect_true(all(c("2-4-2-5", "2-1-3-1") %in% apply(m, 1, paste, collapse = "-")))
  g <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx"); on.exit(unlink(g))
  writexl::write_xlsx(iris[1:2, ], g)
  expect_equal(nrow(.xlsx_merges(g, "Sheet1")), 0L)
  expect_error(.xlsx_merges(f, "nope"), "not found")
})

test_that("merge information keeps genuinely empty header cells empty", {
  h <- data.frame(a = c("W", NA), b = c(NA, "End"), c = c(NA, "Note"))
  m <- cbind(r1 = 5L, c1 = 1L, r2 = 5L, c2 = 2L)        # only A5:B5 is merged
  expect_identical(.combine_headers(h, merges = m, first_row = 5L), c("W", "W_End", "Note"))
  expect_identical(.combine_headers(h), c("W", "W_End", "W_Note"))   # heuristic
  expect_identical(.combine_headers(h, fill = "none"), c("W", "End", "Note"))
  v <- data.frame(a = c("ID", NA, NA), b = c("x", "y", "z"))   # vertical merge A1:A3
  expect_identical(.combine_headers(v, merges = cbind(r1 = 1L, c1 = 1L, r2 = 3L, c2 = 1L)),
                   c("ID", "x_y_z"))
})

test_that("import_xlsx header_fill controls merged-cell handling", {
  f <- mintyr_example("multiheader_test.xlsx")
  last <- function(hf) utils::tail(names(import_xlsx(f, sheet = 1, skip = 1, header_rows = 2,
                                                    header_fill = hf)), 1L)
  expect_identical(last("auto"), "Note")
  expect_identical(last("right"), "Backfat (mm)_Note")
  expect_identical(last("none"), "Note")
  expect_error(import_xlsx(f, header_rows = 2, header_fill = "x"), "header_fill")
})

test_that("import_xlsx validates multi-row header arguments", {
  f <- mintyr_example("multiheader_test.xlsx")
  expect_error(import_xlsx(f, header_rows = 0), "header_rows")
  expect_error(import_xlsx(f, header_rows = 2, col_names = FALSE), "col_names")
  expect_error(import_xlsx(f, sheet = "nope"), "not found")
})

test_that("import_xlsx on_error controls failing files and sheets", {
  f <- mintyr_example("multiheader_test.xlsx")
  bad <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx"); on.exit(unlink(bad))
  writeLines("not a workbook", bad)
  expect_error(import_xlsx(c(f, bad)), "Failed to open 1 of 2")
  expect_warning(res <- import_xlsx(c(f, bad), skip = 1, header_rows = 2,
                                    on_error = "warn"), "skipped")
  expect_identical(unique(res$excel_name), "multiheader_test")
  expect_error(suppressWarnings(import_xlsx(bad, on_error = "warn")), "Failed to open")
  # sheet-level failure: col_types only fits one of two sheet layouts
  g <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx"); on.exit(unlink(g), add = TRUE)
  writexl::write_xlsx(list(ok = data.frame(a = 1, b = 2), bad = data.frame(a = 1)), g)
  expect_warning(res <- import_xlsx(g, on_error = "warn", col_types = c("numeric", "numeric")),
                 "sheet 'bad'")
  expect_identical(unique(res$sheet_name), "ok")
  expect_error(import_xlsx(g, col_types = c("numeric", "numeric")), "1 of 2 sheet")
})
```
